sanitizers.precondition: ellipsoid set with abs(flattening) <= 1/50 (the specified range of the geodesic series solver); any source CRS transformable to it; two points that transform to finite geographic coordinates
sanitizers.invariant: the shortest-path distance between two points does not depend on their order
sanitizers.observation_point: end of measureLine(p1,p2), re-called with (p2,p1) on a private copy
sanitizers.alarm: abs(d(p1,p2) - d(p2,p1)) > 1e-7 m + 1e-12 d (geodesic solver accuracy ~1.5e-8 m; swap is exact)
sanitizers.rationale: every length, perimeter and buffer-distance measurement relies on a metric

sanitizers.precondition: ellipsoid set with abs(flattening) <= 1/50 (the specified range of the geodesic series solver); points transform to finite geographic coordinates; heights taken as zero
sanitizers.invariant: no path on the ellipsoid surface is shorter than the straight 3D chord joining its endpoints (chord computed independently from geocentric Cartesian coordinates)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of measureLine(p1,p2), in the same units as the returned value (metres, before unit conversion)
sanitizers.alarm: d_geodesic < chord - 1e-7 m - 1e-12 chord
sanitizers.rationale: a surface distance below the chord is geometrically impossible and indicates a wrong ellipsoid, unit or coordinate order

sanitizers.precondition: ellipsoid set with abs(flattening) <= 1/50; source CRS geographic and on the ellipsoid datum (no reprojection of p1, p2); p1 != p2; geodesic length below one third of the meridian circumference. A projected source CRS is outside the precondition: the planar map frame is used there
sanitizers.invariant: projecting p1 by the measured distance along the measured bearing reaches p2 (direct problem inverts the inverse problem)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of bearing(p1,p2): d = measureLine, az = bearing, q = measureLineProjected(p1,d,az)
sanitizers.alarm: measureLine(q, p2) > 1e-6 m + 1e-11 d
sanitizers.rationale: azimuth-based tools (project points, offset lines, geodesic lines) assume the two geodesic problems agree

sanitizers.precondition: ellipsoid set with abs(flattening) <= 1/50; ring of at least 3 distinct vertices, closed or open, without self-intersection and spanning less than a hemisphere
sanitizers.invariant: the enclosed area does not depend on where the ring starts or on its orientation
sanitizers.observation_point: end of measurePolygon, re-called with the ring cyclically shifted by n/2 and with the ring reversed
sanitizers.alarm: either variant differs by more than 64 eps a^2 + 1e-9 A (a = semi-major axis; accumulation is at geodesic-solver precision)
sanitizers.rationale: polygon areas must not depend on digitising order

sanitizers.precondition: area unit that is the square of a fixed-length unit in the distance enumeration (metres, kilometres, feet, yards, miles, centimetres, millimetres, nautical miles, inches)
sanitizers.invariant: an area factor is the square of the matching length factor (dimensional consistency)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of fromUnitToUnitFactor for area units
sanitizers.alarm: abs(fA(a2,b2)/fL(a,b)^2 - 1) > 16 eps
sanitizers.rationale: area conversions must be dimensionally consistent with length conversions

sanitizers.precondition: three points whose sine of the angle at any vertex exceeds 1e-3 (not nearly collinear), coordinates of any magnitude
sanitizers.invariant: the returned centre is equidistant from the three points, at the returned radius
sanitizers.observation_point: before returning from circleCenterRadius
sanitizers.alarm: max_i abs(|c - p_i| - r) > 64 eps (|c| + r + max|p_i|) / 1e-3
sanitizers.rationale: arc length, arc interpolation, curve densification and offsetting all build on this fit

sanitizers.precondition: circular string whose arcs all have non-zero finite radius; conditioning: the tolerance includes 64 eps (( max|coord| + r_min ) / r_min + 1 / theta_min) for arc angle theta (near-straight arcs lose relative accuracy eps / theta)
sanitizers.invariant: an arc is no shorter than its chord polyline, and the polyline defect is at most the chord-sagitta bound L (delta^2/24) for the angular step delta
sanitizers.observation_point: end of length(), against curveToLine with the checker's own tolerance (angle 1 degree)
sanitizers.alarm: L_arc < L_poly(1 - 1e-12 - kappa) or L_arc > L_poly(1 + delta^2/24 + 1e-9 + kappa), kappa = 64 eps (( max|coord| + r_min ) / r_min + 1 / theta_min)
sanitizers.rationale: curve lengths feed perimeters, measurements and labelling

sanitizers.precondition: polygon with finite coordinates of at least 3 vertices in the exterior ring
sanitizers.invariant: polygon area does not depend on the ring's starting vertex or orientation
sanitizers.observation_point: end of area(), re-evaluated on the exterior ring cyclically shifted by n/2 and reversed
sanitizers.alarm: difference > 16 n eps sum_i (abs(x_i y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} y_i) + abs(x_i) abs(dy_i) + abs(y_i) abs(dx_i))
sanitizers.rationale: area-based statistics and overlay fractions assume orientation independence

sanitizers.precondition: multipolygon of 2 to 20 valid, mutually disjoint parts, each with area >= 1e-2 of its bounding box (no slivers: the rounding of a centroid scales with extent^2 / area)
sanitizers.invariant: the centroid is the area-weighted mean of the part centroids
sanitizers.observation_point: end of centroid(); parts re-evaluated individually through the same API
sanitizers.alarm: norm(c - sum_i A_i c_i / sum_i A_i) > 1e-9 extent + 64 eps (|c| + extent + max|coord| extent^2 / A_min)
sanitizers.rationale: centre-of-mass calculations (label points, mean centres) depend on this decomposition

sanitizers.precondition: valid simple polygon, any holes (the outer ring perimeter is used)
sanitizers.invariant: among planar regions of a given perimeter the disc has the greatest area: A <= P^2 / (4 pi)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of area(), against an independently summed outer-ring length
sanitizers.alarm: A > P^2 / (4 pi) (1 + 1e-9) + 64 eps n_vertices max|coord| (max|coord| + P) (the area sums products of absolute coordinates)
sanitizers.rationale: an area/length pair violating the isoperimetric bound is geometrically impossible

sanitizers.precondition: valid polygon with linear segments only (curves are buffered through a linearisation that lies below the exact curved area), segments >= 8, default cap and join style, distance d >= 1e-9 extent and d >= 1e6 eps max|coord| (a vanishing distance is returned empty by GEOS)
sanitizers.invariant: enlarging the buffer distance cannot shrink the buffered region, and the buffer contains its source geometry in area
sanitizers.observation_point: end of buffer(d), re-called with 2d on the same inputs
sanitizers.alarm: area(buf(2d)) < area(buf(d)) (1 - 1e-9) or area(buf(d)) < area(geometry) (1 - 1e-9)
sanitizers.rationale: proximity analysis and exclusion zones are monotone in distance

sanitizers.precondition: distance > 0, azimuth in degrees with abs(azimuth) <= 720, distance >= 1e-200 (not subnormal), inclination 90 degrees (planar)
sanitizers.invariant: the azimuth and distance from the origin to the projected point equal the requested azimuth and distance
sanitizers.observation_point: before returning from project
sanitizers.alarm: circular difference of azimuth in degrees > 64 eps (1 + |p|/d) (180/pi) + 1e-12 abs(azimuth), or abs(distance - d) > 64 eps (|p| + d)
sanitizers.rationale: offset, bearing-intersection and geodesic helpers compose these two operations

sanitizers.precondition: direction vectors non-zero with |sin(angle)| > 1e-6
sanitizers.invariant: the returned point lies on both lines
sanitizers.observation_point: before returning true from lineIntersection
sanitizers.alarm: max_i abs(cross(x - p_i, v_i))/|v_i| > 1e3 eps (|x| + |p_1| + |p_2|)/abs(sin)
sanitizers.rationale: snapping, topology and offset algorithms assume the point lies on the lines

sanitizers.precondition: at least one finite value with max|x| <= 1e150 (sums and midpoints must not overflow), all requested statistics
sanitizers.invariant: minimum <= first quartile <= median <= third quartile <= maximum and minimum <= mean <= maximum (requires the median and both quartiles to be requested)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of finalize()
sanitizers.alarm: any ordered pair violated by more than 8 eps max|x|, or the mean outside [min, max] by more than 8 n eps max|x|
sanitizers.rationale: summary tables and outlier fences assume a consistent quantile ordering

sanitizers.precondition: n >= 2 finite values with 0 < max|x| <= 1e150; shift c with abs(c) <= 10 max|x| and mean^2/variance <= 1e4 for x and x + c
sanitizers.invariant: the summary does not depend on input order, mean and quantiles shift by c, variance and range do not change
sanitizers.observation_point: end of finalize(), on a private summary fed the reversed list and the shifted list
sanitizers.alarm: median/quartiles/range differ by more than 8 eps max|x + c|; mean by more than 8 n eps max|x + c|; variance by more than 64 n eps (var + mean^2/1e4)
sanitizers.rationale: reported statistics are properties of the sample, not of its ordering or origin

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata, mCellSizeX == mCellSizeY, finite z-factor
sanitizers.invariant: slope is a property of the surface, so rotating the window by 90 degrees leaves it unchanged
sanitizers.observation_point: end of processNineCellWindow, re-called with the window rotated 90 degrees
sanitizers.alarm: abs(s - s_rot) > 1e-4 degrees + 100 eps32 max|z| zfactor/cell
sanitizers.rationale: slope maps must not depend on raster orientation

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata whose gradient is non-zero (gradient magnitude > 100 eps32 max|z|/cell)
sanitizers.invariant: mirroring the window east-west maps aspect a to 360 - a (modulo 360)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of processNineCellWindow, re-called with the window mirrored
sanitizers.alarm: circular difference between a' and 360 - a exceeds 1e-3 degrees + 1e3 eps32 max|z|/(cell gradient)
sanitizers.rationale: aspect is a compass direction of steepest descent and must transform as one

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata; shift c with abs(c) <= 10 max|z| so that no shifted cell equals the input nodata value
sanitizers.invariant: terrain derivatives depend on elevation differences, not absolute elevation
sanitizers.observation_point: end of each filter's processNineCellWindow, re-called with every cell shifted by c
sanitizers.alarm: difference > per-product tolerance, each with the output's own float rounding 4 eps32 abs(result): slope (degrees) 1e-4 + 64 (180/pi) eps32 (max|z| + abs(c)) abs(zf) / cell_min; aspect (degrees, only if gradient > 1e3 times its rounding error) 1e-3 + (180/pi) err_g / g; hillshade (0..255) 255 (64 eps32 + 8 eps32 (max|z| + abs(c)) abs(zf) / cell_min) + 1e-3; ruggedness (elevation units, no cell size) 64 eps32 (max|z| + abs(c)); curvature 4 e (sqrt(abs(a)) + e), e = 64 eps32 (max|z| + abs(c)) / cell^2
sanitizers.rationale: a uniform vertical datum change must not change slope, shade or roughness

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata, any light azimuth and any light angle in (0, 90] (vertical angle of the sun above the horizon)
sanitizers.invariant: illumination is Lambert's cosine law: 255 max(0, n.s) for the surface normal n from an independent double-precision Horn gradient and the unit sun vector s (azimuth clockwise from north; the light angle is the sun altitude above the horizon as in QgsHillshadeRenderer, the processing algorithm (Vertical angle) and the GDAL convention, so zenith = 90 - angle)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of processNineCellWindow
sanitizers.alarm: abs(h - 255 max(0, n.s)) > 255 (64 eps32 + 8 eps32 max|z|/cell) + 1e-3
sanitizers.rationale: hillshading is a physical illumination model and must agree with the cosine law

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata whose nine cells are exactly planar to 8 eps32 max|z| (least-squares residual)
sanitizers.invariant: the Horn operator recovers a plane's gradient exactly: derX = a zfactor and derY = b zfactor
sanitizers.observation_point: end of calcFirstDerX / calcFirstDerY
sanitizers.alarm: abs(derX - a zfactor) or abs(derY - b zfactor) > 64 eps32 max|z| zfactor/cell
sanitizers.rationale: slope and aspect are exact for planar terrain by construction of the operator

sanitizers.precondition: window without nodata, max|z| <= 1e15; ruggedness or total curvature either 0 or >= 1e-12 in magnitude (float32 squares must not underflow); scaling factor exactly 2 (exact in binary floating point), 2z not equal to nodata and finite
sanitizers.invariant: ruggedness is homogeneous of degree 1 in elevation and total curvature of degree 2
sanitizers.observation_point: end of processNineCellWindow, re-called with 2z
sanitizers.alarm: abs(R(2z) - 2 R(z)) > 16 eps32 R(z) or abs(K(2z) - 4 K(z)) > 16 eps32 K(z)
sanitizers.rationale: roughness has units of length and curvature of 1/length^2; scaling elevation must scale them accordingly

sanitizers.precondition: coefficient in (0, 10], finite data, query away from every node, and abs(z)max / d_min^p < 1e150 (the implementation sums z / d^p unscaled, which must not overflow double)
sanitizers.invariant: a convex combination of data values lies between the smallest and largest datum
sanitizers.observation_point: before returning from interpolatePoint
sanitizers.alarm: v < z_min - 8 n eps max|z| or v > z_max + 8 n eps max|z|
sanitizers.rationale: an interpolated elevation or concentration outside the observed range is not an interpolation

sanitizers.precondition: linear interpolation method; the cached vertices are coplanar to 64 eps max(|z|, extent); query inside the hull; tolerance 1e3 eps scale (1 + max|coord| / extent), the factor covering cancellation at large absolute coordinates
sanitizers.invariant: a piecewise-linear interpolant reproduces a plane exactly
sanitizers.observation_point: before returning from interpolatePoint
sanitizers.alarm: abs(v - (a x + b y + c)) > 1e3 eps (max|z| + |a| extent + |b| extent)
sanitizers.rationale: TIN surfaces of planar terrain must be planar

sanitizers.precondition: linear or Helmert transform with parameters fitted (projective and polynomial transforms are outside this check); scale above 1024 eps; point finite
sanitizers.invariant: transforming then inverse-transforming a point returns it
sanitizers.observation_point: end of transform() on a private re-evaluation of the inverse
sanitizers.alarm: norm(T^-1 T p - p) > 1e3 eps cond (|p| + |T p| + |origin|) max(1, s_max)/min(1, s_min); cond = s_max/s_min (1 for similarity)
sanitizers.rationale: pixel-to-map and map-to-pixel conversions must be mutually inverse

sanitizers.precondition: at least two ground control points with non-coincident sources (cond = sum|src|^2 / sum|src - mean|^2 is finite); linear fit: each axis has positive variance of the sources (the API returns the magnitude of the slope, so the sign is taken from the data covariance)
sanitizers.invariant: the fitted parameters are a stationary point of the sum of squared residuals (normal equations hold)
sanitizers.observation_point: end of helmert() and of linear()
sanitizers.alarm: norm(grad SSE) > 1e3 eps cond sum|terms|
sanitizers.rationale: a transform that is not the least-squares optimum biases every georeferenced coordinate

sanitizers.precondition: at least two non-coincident sources, translation t with |t| <= 10 (extent + |centre|) and normal-equation conditioning below 1e10
sanitizers.invariant: translating all destination points translates the fitted origin and leaves scale and rotation unchanged
sanitizers.observation_point: end of helmert(), re-called with destinations + t
sanitizers.alarm: abs(scale' - scale) > dS or circular abs(rot' - rot) > dS / scale or norm(origin' - origin - t) > 1e3 eps cond (|t| + |origin| + max|dst|) + dS max|src|, dS = 1e3 eps cond (max|dst| + |t|) / extent_src (destination rounding eps |dst| / extent_src included)
sanitizers.rationale: a georeferencing fit must not depend on the datum origin chosen

sanitizers.precondition: Scaled output values, any shape, any bandwidth in [1e-100, 1e12] (below that the normalisation overflows), triangular decay >= 0
sanitizers.invariant: the kernel is a probability density on the plane: integral of K(d) 2 pi d dd over [0, bandwidth] equals 1 (independent 64-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature in d)
sanitizers.observation_point: first call for each (shape, bandwidth, decay), cached per triple
sanitizers.alarm: abs(integral - 1) > 1e-9
sanitizers.rationale: a density surface integrates to the point count only if each kernel integrates to one

sanitizers.precondition: any shape, bandwidth in [1e-100, 1e12], triangular decay in [0, 1] (for decay > 1 the triangular kernel increases with distance)
sanitizers.invariant: a density kernel is non-negative and non-increasing in distance on [0, bandwidth]
sanitizers.observation_point: same observation as QG-KDE-001, probed at 17 distances
sanitizers.rationale: a hot-spot map must not increase away from the point

sanitizers.precondition: source and destination are geographic or projected CRS (longitude compared modulo 360 degrees), operation without a grid shift missing, point inside both areas of use and 1 degree away from a projection singularity, not ballpark
sanitizers.invariant: forward then reverse transformation returns the original coordinates
sanitizers.observation_point: end of transform(), on a private reverse transform
sanitizers.alarm: distance(p, T^-1 T p) > 5e-2 m (metres, or degrees converted at the point's latitude); 5 cm is the second-order error bound theta^2 R of small-angle datum-shift operations (theta <= 5e-5 rad)
sanitizers.rationale: a layer reprojected twice must return to its source coordinates

sanitizers.precondition: valid, finite rectangle inside the source CRS area of use; geographic destinations only when the result is below 90 degrees wide and below 85 degrees of latitude (wrap-around excluded)
sanitizers.invariant: the transformed bounding box encloses the transformed corners and edge midpoints
sanitizers.observation_point: end of transformBoundingBox
sanitizers.alarm: any sampled point outside the box by more than 1e-3 box size (the box is built from sampled boundary points, so an edge can bulge between samples)
sanitizers.rationale: extents of reprojected layers must contain their data
